chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from 'Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed usury, and its eater, its seller, its buyer, its scribe, and its two witnesses.
ai.seo_question: Who are the parties cursed in Islam for dealing with usury (riba)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from the Prophet via Imam Ali emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the riba prohibition by cursing not only the primary parties but also the scribe and witnesses, establishing their equal culpability in the transaction. This inclusion of secondary participants underscores the jurisprudential principle that all elements facilitating the usurious contract are subject to the same divine decree, reinforcing the severity of the sin in Shia legal tradition.
